top_3_concealment_risks.risk: NOI deliberately hidden behind login wall
top_3_concealment_risks.detail: LoopNet typically shows NOI/cap rate for income properties. Its absence suggests either very low NOI or the seller/broker doesn't want buyers to see the real cap rate before engaging. The fact that assessment is $117,900 and they're asking $799,000 means any cap rate based on stale taxes is fictitious.

top_3_concealment_risks.risk: In-place rent well below market — tenants are under-market
top_3_concealment_risks.detail: The 'buyer can occupy one or two units' language implies at least one tenant may be leaving or on month-to-month. If current rents are below market, the listing agent would advertise the mark-to-market upside. Its absence is suspicious.

Class C, 1924 construction, no renovation year mentioned. Roof, HVAC, electrical, and plumbing are likely near end-of-life. The 'RECENT PRICE REDUCTION' may partially reflect deferred capex the seller is unwilling to fund.

lawyer_brain.tax_bomb_flag: Assessment is $117,900 vs ask $799,000 — post-sale taxes will jump from ~$2,830/yr to ~$19,176/yr. This is the #1 risk to tenant retention under NNN leases.
